  4180	a nonzero covariance satisfying `H:homog` with `a = alpha0`; the wrappers

  4193	root of the supremum of the real Rayleigh values of `m_R h_s` (the convention
  4194	of `rate`); `int_I lambda_(R,s) ds`; and the named input

  4196	
  4197	The rate part is proved with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied
  4198	(`variational_remove_mask_rates_paper`): the masks form an increasing family
  4199	of admissible radial masks tending to one (`mask_family`, lines 184-191), a

  4201	`lambda_(R,s) <= lambda_(R',s) <= lambda_(Psi,s)` for `0 < R <= R'`, a Lipschitz
  4202	bound in `s`, the exchange of suprema (lines 200-206), pointwise and uniform
  4203	convergence on `I` (lines 207-211), and `int_I lambda_(R,s) ds` nondecreasing,
  4204	at most `I_Psi` and tending to `I_Psi` (line 212). The display

    72	
    73	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `I = [0,1]`; "uniformly on `I`" is
    74	`TendstoUniformlyOn` on `Icc 0 1`; finiteness of the suprema is stated as
    75	nonempty bounded-above value sets; integrability of `λ_{R,·}` on `(0,1)`
    76	is part of the conclusion; the liminf is taken in `EReal`, so it is never a
    77	junk value.  The TeX's masks have `R > 0`; for `R ≤ 0` the Lean definition
    78	gives `m_R ≡ 1` (division convention at `R = 0`, sign for `R < 0`), and the
    79	smoothness, plateau, support and monotonicity statements assume `R > 0`
    80	(continuity, the `[0,1]` bounds, radiality and evenness hold for every `R`).
    81	
    82	Proof routes that differ from the TeX:
    83	* Common margin: the TeX uses the compact trial of
    84	  `P:compact-original-common-trial` (line 193).  Here the trial is the test
    85	  function of `VariationalFloor.dilation_floor` (the route of
    86	  `VariationalRate.unmasked_rate`), supported in a ball of radius `R₁`;
    87	  `R₀ = R₁ + 1`, and for `R ≥ R₀` its masked and unmasked Rayleigh values
    88	  coincide.
    89	* Exchange of suprema: proved as convergence of the suprema as `R → ∞`
    90	  (dominated convergence for each fixed trial, lines 197-199), from which the
    91	  supremum over `R ≥ R₀` follows by monotonicity.
    92	* Uniform convergence: Mathlib's Dini theorem
    93	  (`Monotone.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_forall_tendsto`) applied to the monotone
    94	  family `R ↦ λ_{max(R,R₀),s}` of continuous functions on `I`, which equals
    95	  `λ_{R,s}` for `R ≥ R₀`; the TeX runs the finite-subcover argument along
    96	  `R_n = R₀ + n` and extends by monotonicity (lines 208-211).
    97	* `∫_I λ_{R,s} ds → I_Ψ`: dominated convergence with the bound `√M`; the TeX
    98	  deduces it from the uniform convergence (line 212).
    99	Lemmas marked "Auxiliary to the Lean proof route" have no manuscript label.
   100	-/

   131	/-! ### The profile `χ` and the masks `m_R` -/
   132	
   133	/-- The TeX's `F` (line 182): `F(t) = e^{-1/t}` for `t > 0` and `0` otherwise
   134	is Mathlib's `expNegInvGlue`. -/
   135	theorem expNegInvGlue_eq (t : ℝ) :
   136	    expNegInvGlue t = if t ≤ 0 then 0 else Real.exp (-(1 / t)) := by
   137	  rw [one_div]; rfl
   138	
   139	/-- The profile of the masks (TeX line 184), `χ(r) = smoothTransition(2 - r)`. -/
   140	def chi (r : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.smoothTransition (2 - r)
   141	
   142	/-- `χ` is the TeX's quotient: `χ(r) = F(2-r)/(F(2-r) + F(r-1))` (line 184). -/
   143	theorem chi_eq (r : ℝ) :
   144	    chi r = expNegInvGlue (2 - r) / (expNegInvGlue (2 - r) + expNegInvGlue (r - 1)) := by
   145	  unfold chi Real.smoothTransition
   146	  rw [show (1 : ℝ) - (2 - r) = r - 1 by ring]
   147	
   148	/-- The denominator of `χ` is positive (line 187). -/
   149	theorem chi_denom_pos (r : ℝ) : 0 < expNegInvGlue (2 - r) + expNegInvGlue (r - 1) := by
   150	  have := Real.smoothTransition.pos_denom (2 - r)
   151	  rwa [show (1 : ℝ) - (2 - r) = r - 1 by ring] at this
   152	
   153	/-- `χ` is nonincreasing (lines 187-188). -/
   154	theorem chi_antitone : Antitone chi := fun _ _ hab =>
   155	  Real.smoothTransition.monotone (by linarith)
   156	
   157	/-- `χ = 1` on `r ≤ 1` (line 188). -/
   158	theorem chi_eq_one {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≤ 1) : chi r = 1 :=
   159	  Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le (by linarith)
   160	
   161	/-- `χ = 0` on `r ≥ 2` (line 189). -/
   162	theorem chi_eq_zero {r : ℝ} (hr : 2 ≤ r) : chi r = 0 :=
   163	  Real.smoothTransition.zero_of_nonpos (by linarith)
   164	
   165	/-- `0 ≤ χ ≤ 1` (line 191). -/
   166	theorem chi_mem (r : ℝ) : 0 ≤ chi r ∧ chi r ≤ 1 :=
   167	  ⟨Real.smoothTransition.nonneg _, Real.smoothTransition.le_one _⟩
   168	
   169	/-- `χ` is smooth (line 189). -/
   170	theorem chi_contDiff : ContDiff ℝ ∞ chi :=
   171	  Real.smoothTransition.contDiff.comp (contDiff_const.sub contDiff_id)
   172	
   173	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `χ` is continuous. -/
   174	theorem chi_continuous : Continuous chi :=
   175	  Real.smoothTransition.continuous.comp (continuous_const.sub continuous_id)
   176	
   177	/-- The masks of the TeX (line 185): `m_R(x) = χ(|x|/R)`.  (For `R = 0`
   178	Lean's division convention, and for `R < 0` the sign, make `m_R ≡ 1`; the
   179	smoothness, plateau, support and monotonicity statements below assume
   180	`R > 0`, the limits concern `R → ∞`.) -/
   181	def mask (R : ℝ) (x : Rd d) : ℝ := chi (‖x‖ / R)
   182	
   183	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `m_R` is continuous (every `R`). -/
   184	theorem mask_continuous (R : ℝ) : Continuous (mask (d := d) R) :=
   185	  chi_continuous.comp (continuous_norm.div_const R)
   186	
   187	/-- `0 ≤ m_R ≤ 1` (line 191). -/
   188	theorem mask_mem (R : ℝ) (x : Rd d) : 0 ≤ mask R x ∧ mask R x ≤ 1 := chi_mem _
   189	
   190	/-- `m_R` is radial (line 170). -/
   191	theorem mask_radial (R : ℝ) {x y : Rd d} (h : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖) : mask R x = mask R y := by
   192	  simp only [mask, h]
   193	
   194	/-- `m_R` is even (line 191). -/
   195	theorem mask_neg (R : ℝ) (x : Rd d) : mask R (-x) = mask R x := by
   196	  simp only [mask, norm_neg]
   197	
   198	/-- `m_R = 1` on the closed ball `|x| ≤ R` (from line 188). -/
   199	theorem mask_eq_one {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) {x : Rd d} (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ R) : mask R x = 1 :=
   200	  chi_eq_one ((div_le_one hR).2 hx)
   201	
   202	/-- `m_R = 0` on `|x| ≥ 2R` (from line 189). -/
   203	theorem mask_eq_zero {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) {x : Rd d} (hx : 2 * R ≤ ‖x‖) : mask R x = 0 :=
   204	  chi_eq_zero ((le_div_iff₀ hR).2 hx)
   205	
   206	/-- The support of `m_R` lies in the closed ball of radius `2R` (from line
   207	189). -/
   208	theorem tsupport_mask_subset {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) :
   209	    tsupport (mask (d := d) R) ⊆ closedBall 0 (2 * R) := by
   210	  refine closure_minimal (fun x hx => ?_) isClosed_closedBall
   211	  by_contra h
   212	  rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right, not_le] at h
   213	  exact hx (mask_eq_zero hR h.le)
   214	
   215	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `m_R` has compact support. -/
   216	theorem mask_hasCompactSupport {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) : HasCompactSupport (mask (d := d) R) :=
   217	  (isCompact_closedBall 0 (2 * R)).of_isClosed_subset (isClosed_tsupport _)
   218	    (tsupport_mask_subset hR)
   219	
   220	/-- `m_R` is smooth for `R > 0`, also at the origin, where it is constant
   221	(lines 189-190). -/
   222	theorem mask_contDiff {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (mask (d := d) R) := by
   223	  rw [contDiff_iff_contDiffAt]
   224	  intro x
   225	  by_cases hx : x = 0
   226	  · have : (mask (d := d) R) =ᶠ[𝓝 x] fun _ => 1 := by
   227	      filter_upwards [ball_mem_nhds x hR] with y hy
   228	      rw [hx, mem_ball, dist_zero_right] at hy
   229	      exact mask_eq_one hR hy.le
   230	    exact contDiffAt_const.congr_of_eventuallyEq this
   231	  · exact chi_contDiff.contDiffAt.comp x ((contDiffAt_norm ℝ hx).div_const R)
   232	
   233	/-- The masks increase in `R > 0` (line 191). -/
   234	theorem mask_mono {R R' : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (hRR : R ≤ R') (x : Rd d) :
   235	    mask R x ≤ mask R' x :=
   236	  chi_antitone (div_le_div_of_nonneg_left (norm_nonneg x) hR hRR)
   237	
   238	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: at every point, `m_R = 1` for all
   239	large `R`. -/
   240	theorem mask_eventually_one (x : Rd d) : ∀ᶠ R in atTop, mask R x = 1 := by
   241	  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (max ‖x‖ 1)] with R hR
   242	  exact mask_eq_one (lt_of_lt_of_le one_pos ((le_max_right _ _).trans hR))
   243	    ((le_max_left _ _).trans hR)
   244	
   245	/-- The masks tend to one pointwise (line 191). -/
   246	theorem mask_tendsto (x : Rd d) : Tendsto (fun R => mask R x) atTop (𝓝 1) :=
   247	  tendsto_const_nhds.congr' ((mask_eventually_one x).mono fun _ h => h.symm)

   249	/-! ### Rayleigh value sets: comparison and the exchange of suprema -/
   250	
   251	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the Rayleigh value set of a potential
   252	with `V f²` integrable for every `f ∈ L²` is nonempty (the unit test
   253	`VariationalFloor.fl 1` is a trial). -/
   254	theorem rayleighSet_nonempty {V : Rd d → ℝ}
   255	    (hV : ∀ f : Rd d → ℝ, MemLp f 2 volume → Integrable (fun x => V x * f x ^ 2) volume) :
   256	    (rayleighSet V).Nonempty :=
   257	  ⟨_, fl 1, gl 1, ⟨memLp_test (fl_test one_pos), gl_memLp one_pos, gl_weak one_pos,
   258	    fl_unit one_pos, hV _ (memLp_test (fl_test one_pos))⟩, rfl⟩
   259	
   260	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  Comparison of Rayleigh values: if `V ≤ W` pointwise, `W f²` is integrable

261	for every `f ∈ L²` and the value set of `W` is bounded above, then every
   262	Rayleigh value of `V` is at most `sup R_W`. -/
   263	theorem rayleighValue_le_sSup_of_le {V W : Rd d → ℝ} (hVW : ∀ x, V x ≤ W x)
   264	    (hW : ∀ f : Rd d → ℝ, MemLp f 2 volume → Integrable (fun x => W x * f x ^ 2) volume)
   265	    (hbW : BddAbove (rayleighSet W)) {q : ℝ} (hq : q ∈ rayleighSet V) :
   266	    q ≤ sSup (rayleighSet W) := by
   267	  obtain ⟨f, g, hT, rfl⟩ := hq
   268	  have hTW : IsRayleighTrial W f g :=
   269	    ⟨hT.memLp_f, hT.memLp_g, hT.weakGrad, hT.unit, hW f hT.memLp_f⟩
   270	  refine le_trans ?_ (le_csSup hbW ⟨f, g, hTW, rfl⟩)
   271	  unfold rayleighValue
   272	  have : ∫ x, V x * f x ^ 2 ≤ ∫ x, W x * f x ^ 2 :=
   273	    integral_mono hT.integrable_pot hTW.integrable_pot
   274	      fun x => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hVW x) (sq_nonneg _)
   275	  linarith
   276	
   277	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  Monotonicity of the Rayleigh
   278	supremum in the potential: if `V ≤ W`
   279	pointwise, both `V f²` and `W f²` are integrable for every `f ∈ L²`, and the
   280	value set of `W` is bounded above, then the value set of `V` is nonempty and
   281	bounded above and `sup R_V ≤ sup R_W`. -/
   282	theorem sSup_rayleighSet_mono {V W : Rd d → ℝ} (hVW : ∀ x, V x ≤ W x)
   283	    (hV : ∀ f : Rd d → ℝ, MemLp f 2 volume → Integrable (fun x => V x * f x ^ 2) volume)
   284	    (hW : ∀ f : Rd d → ℝ, MemLp f 2 volume → Integrable (fun x => W x * f x ^ 2) volume)
   285	    (hbW : BddAbove (rayleighSet W)) :
   286	    (rayleighSet V).Nonempty ∧ BddAbove (rayleighSet V) ∧
   287	      sSup (rayleighSet V) ≤ sSup (rayleighSet W) :=
   288	  ⟨rayleighSet_nonempty hV, ⟨_, fun _ hq => rayleighValue_le_sSup_of_le hVW hW hbW hq⟩,
   289	    csSup_le (rayleighSet_nonempty hV) fun _ hq => rayleighValue_le_sSup_of_le hVW hW hbW hq⟩
   290	
   291	/-- The exchange of the two suprema (TeX lines 197-207) for a general family
   292	of potentials.  Let `V_i ≤ W` pointwise, `|V_i| ≤ B`, `V_i → W` pointwise
   293	along a countably generated filter, with `V_i f²` and `W f²` integrable for
   294	every `f ∈ L²`, and the value set of `W` nonempty and bounded above.  Then
   295	`sup R_{V_i} → sup R_W`.  (For each fixed unit `f`, dominated convergence
   296	gives `∫ V_i f² → ∫ W f²`.) -/
   297	theorem tendsto_sSup_rayleighSet {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [l.IsCountablyGenerated]
   298	    {V : ι → Rd d → ℝ} {W : Rd d → ℝ} {B : ℝ}
   299	    (hV : ∀ i, ∀ f : Rd d → ℝ, MemLp f 2 volume →
   300	      Integrable (fun x => V i x * f x ^ 2) volume)
   301	    (hW : ∀ f : Rd d → ℝ, MemLp f 2 volume → Integrable (fun x => W x * f x ^ 2) volume)
   302	    (hle : ∀ i x, V i x ≤ W x) (hB : ∀ i x, |V i x| ≤ B)
   303	    (hlim : ∀ x, Tendsto (fun i => V i x) l (𝓝 (W x)))
   304	    (hneW : (rayleighSet W).Nonempty) (hbW : BddAbove (rayleighSet W)) :
   305	    Tendsto (fun i => sSup (rayleighSet (V i))) l (𝓝 (sSup (rayleighSet W))) := by
   306	  have hmono := fun i => sSup_rayleighSet_mono (hle i) (hV i) hW hbW
   307	  refine tendsto_order.2 ⟨fun b hb => ?_, fun b hb => ?_⟩
   308	  · obtain ⟨q, ⟨f, g, hT, rfl⟩, hbq⟩ := exists_lt_of_lt_csSup hneW hb
   309	    have hf := hT.memLp_f
   310	    have hDCT : Tendsto (fun i => ∫ x, V i x * f x ^ 2) l (𝓝 (∫ x, W x * f x ^ 2)) := by
   311	      refine tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence (fun x => B * f x ^ 2)
   312	        (Eventually.of_forall fun i => (hV i f hf).aestronglyMeasurable)
   313	        (Eventually.of_forall fun i => ae_of_all _ fun x => ?_)
   314	        (hf.integrable_sq.const_mul B) (ae_of_all _ fun x => (hlim x).mul_const _)
   315	      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg (f x))]
   316	      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hB i x) (sq_nonneg _)
   317	    have hval : Tendsto (fun i => rayleighValue (V i) f g) l (𝓝 (rayleighValue W f g)) :=
   318	      hDCT.sub_const _
   319	    filter_upwards [hval.eventually (lt_mem_nhds hbq)] with i hi
   320	    have hTi : IsRayleighTrial (V i) f g :=
   321	      ⟨hT.memLp_f, hT.memLp_g, hT.weakGrad, hT.unit, hV i f hf⟩
   322	    exact lt_of_lt_of_le hi (le_csSup (hmono i).2.1 ⟨f, g, hTi, rfl⟩)
   323	  · exact Eventually.of_forall fun i => lt_of_le_of_lt (hmono i).2.2 hb
   324	
   325	/-! ### The masked means and rates -/
   326	
   327	/-- The masked mean `m_R h_{Ψ,s}`. -/
   328	def maskedMean (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) (R s : ℝ) (x : Rd d) : ℝ :=
   329	  mask R x * mean a Γ Ψ s x
   330	
   331	/-- The masked rate `λ_{R,s} = √(sup of the real Rayleigh values of m_R h_s)`
   332	(the Rayleigh convention of `VariationalDilation.rate`). -/
   333	def maskedRate (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) (R s : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   334	  rayleighRate (maskedMean a Γ Ψ R s)
   335	
   336	/-- `∫_0^1 λ_{R,s} ds`. -/
   337	def maskedIntegratedRate (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) (R : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   338	  ∫ s in Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, maskedRate a Γ Ψ R s
   339	
   340	/-- **`P:variational-remove-mask`, rate part, general form** (TeX lines
   341	168-174 and 193-212).  For tempered `Γ`, `μ` with the spectral convention,
   342	`Γ` nonzero and locally finite with the set scaling of `H:homog`, `α < 2`,
   343	`0 ≤ a < 1` and `Ψ ∈ CPos`: there are reals `ε > 0`, `M ≥ ε`, `C ≥ 0`,
   344	`R₀ > 0` such that (i) for `R ≥ R₀` and `s ∈ [0,1]` the Rayleigh value set
   345	of `m_R h_s` is nonempty and bounded above, `ε ≤ λ_{R,s}² = sup ≤ M` and
   346	`√ε ≤ λ_{R,s} ≤ √M`; (ii) for `s ∈ [0,1]` and `0 < R ≤ R'`,
   347	`λ_{R,s} ≤ λ_{R',s} ≤ λ_{Ψ,s}`; (iii) for `R ≥ R₀`,
   348	`|λ_{R,s} - λ_{R,t}| ≤ C/(2√ε) |s - t|` on `[0,1]`; (iv) for `s ∈ [0,1]`,
   349	the supremum over `R ≥ R₀` of the suprema of the value sets of `m_R h_s` is
   350	the supremum of the value set of `h_s`; (v) `λ_{R,s} → λ_{Ψ,s}` as
   351	`R → ∞` for `s ∈ [0,1]`; (vi) uniformly on `[0,1]`; (vii) for `R ≥ R₀`,
   352	`λ_{R,·}` is integrable on `(0,1)`, `∫_0^1 λ_{R,s} ds` is nondecreasing in
   353	`R ≥ R₀` and at most `I_Ψ`, and it tends to `I_Ψ`.  Route differences: see
   354	the module doc. -/
   355	theorem remove_mask {alpha : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓt : IsTempered Γ)
   356	    (hμt : IsTempered μ) (hsp : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ]
   357	    (hS : SetScaling alpha Γ) (hα : alpha < 2) (hΓ : Γ ≠ 0) {a : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha : a < 1)
   358	    {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Ψ ∈ CPos d) :
   359	    ∃ ε M C R₀ : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε ≤ M ∧ 0 ≤ C ∧ 0 < R₀ ∧
   360	      (∀ R, R₀ ≤ R → ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
   361	        (rayleighSet (maskedMean a Γ Ψ R s)).Nonempty ∧
   362	        BddAbove (rayleighSet (maskedMean a Γ Ψ R s)) ∧
   363	        ε ≤ sSup (rayleighSet (maskedMean a Γ Ψ R s)) ∧
   364	        sSup (rayleighSet (maskedMean a Γ Ψ R s)) ≤ M ∧
   365	        maskedRate a Γ Ψ R s ^ 2 = sSup (rayleighSet (maskedMean a Γ Ψ R s)) ∧
   366	        Real.sqrt ε ≤ maskedRate a Γ Ψ R s ∧ maskedRate a Γ Ψ R s ≤ Real.sqrt M) ∧
   367	      (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ R R', 0 < R → R ≤ R' →
   368	        maskedRate a Γ Ψ R s ≤ maskedRate a Γ Ψ R' s ∧
   369	        maskedRate a Γ Ψ R' s ≤ rate a Γ Ψ s) ∧
   370	      (∀ R, R₀ ≤ R → ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
   371	        |maskedRate a Γ Ψ R s - maskedRate a Γ Ψ R t| ≤
   372	          C / (2 * Real.sqrt ε) * |s - t|) ∧
   373	      (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
   374	        sSup ((fun R => sSup (rayleighSet (maskedMean a Γ Ψ R s))) '' Ici R₀) =
   375	          sSup (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s))) ∧
   376	      (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
   377	        Tendsto (fun R => maskedRate a Γ Ψ R s) atTop (𝓝 (rate a Γ Ψ s))) ∧
   378	      TendstoUniformlyOn (fun R s => maskedRate a Γ Ψ R s) (rate a Γ Ψ) atTop (Icc 0 1) ∧
   379	      (∀ R, R₀ ≤ R → IntegrableOn (maskedRate a Γ Ψ R) (Ioo 0 1)) ∧
   380	      (∀ R R', R₀ ≤ R → R ≤ R' →
   381	        maskedIntegratedRate a Γ Ψ R ≤ maskedIntegratedRate a Γ Ψ R' ∧
   382	        maskedIntegratedRate a Γ Ψ R' ≤ integratedRate a Γ Ψ) ∧
   383	      Tendsto (maskedIntegratedRate a Γ Ψ) atTop (𝓝 (integratedRate a Γ Ψ)) := by
   384	  -- the unmasked rate and the mean

   840	  117|   densely defined, symmetric and closed on $H^2$; the two graph norms are

    69	/-- Consumer of the two wrappers: if the order bounds of
    70	`static_phase_all_orders_paper` hold for every `n ≥ 1` (as norms of the phases `Z n`)
    71	together with the free bound for `Z 0`, then `E:all-static-phase-sum` holds. -/
    72	private theorem audit_consumer {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    73	    [CompleteSpace E] (Z : ℕ → E) {alpha R h σ N : ℝ}
    74	    (μ Γ : Measure (HomogHypothesis.Rd 3))
    75	    (hμ : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ) (hΓ : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ)
    76	    (hα0 : 0 < alpha) (hα2 : alpha < 2)
    77	    (hRdef : R = alpha * Real.pi * (μ (Metric.ball 0 1)).toReal /
    78	      (2 * Real.sin (Real.pi * alpha / 2)))
    79	    (hh : 0 < h) (hZ0 : ‖Z 0‖ ≤ √(Real.exp 1) * N)
    80	    (hZ : ∀ n, 1 ≤ n → ‖Z n‖ ≤ (allOrdersA alpha * √R) ^ n * h ^ ((4 - alpha) * n / 2) /
    81	      (n ! : ℝ) ^ ((3 - alpha) / 2) * N) :
    82	    ‖∑' n, σ ^ n • Z n‖ ^ 2 ≤ (√(Real.exp 1) + 2) ^ 2 *
    83	        Real.exp (6 * allOrdersA alpha ^ (2 / (3 - alpha)) * (|σ| ^ 2 * R) ^ (1 / (3 - alpha)) *
    84	          h ^ ((4 - alpha) / (3 - alpha))) * N ^ 2 :=
    85	  (all_static_phase_sum_paper Z μ Γ hμ hΓ hα0 hα2 hRdef hh hZ0 hZ).2.2

    30	/-- Euclidean space `ℝ^d`. -/
    31	abbrev Rd (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
    32	
    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    35	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))) ∂ν < ⊤
    36	
    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/
    38	def IsEven {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    39	  ν.map (fun x => -x) = ν
    40	
    41	/-- Positive-definiteness of `Γ` as a tempered distribution:
    42	`⟨Γ, φ ⋆ φ̃⟩` is a nonnegative real for every Schwartz `φ`, where
    43	`(φ ⋆ φ̃)(x) = ∫ φ(x + y) conj(φ(y)) dy` and `φ̃(x) = conj(φ(-x))`. -/
    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re
    48	
    49	/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `Γ` in the manuscript's convention
    50	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)` in the sense of tempered distributions:
    51	`∫ φ dΓ = ∫ (∫ φ(x) e^{i ξ·x} dx) μ(dξ)` for every Schwartz `φ`. -/
    52	def IsSpectralMeasure {d : ℕ} (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    53	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =
    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ
    56	
    57	/-- Hypothesis `H:homog`. Let `d ∈ {1,2,3}` and `0 < α₀ < 1`. The spatial
    58	covariance is a nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure
    59	`Γ` on `ℝ^d` with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure `μ`,
    60	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)`; for every Borel set `A` and `c > 0`,
    61	`Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`; `α₀ + α < 2` (`E:threshold`), with `0 < α < d` or
    62	`α = d = 1`. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on `ℝ^d` a locally finite
    63	Borel measure is a Radon measure. -/
    64	structure HomogCovariance (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) :
    65	    Prop where
    66	  dim : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3
    67	  alpha0_pos : 0 < alpha0
    68	  alpha0_lt_one : alpha0 < 1
    69	  Γ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ
    70	  Γ_even : IsEven Γ
    71	  Γ_tempered : IsTempered Γ
    72	  Γ_posdef : IsPosDefDistr Γ
    73	  μ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ
    74	  μ_even : IsEven μ
    75	  μ_tempered : IsTempered μ
    76	  spectral : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ
    77	  scaling : ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
    78	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
    79	  threshold : alpha0 + alpha < 2
    80	  alpha_range : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)
    81	
    82	/-- The numerical part of `H:homog`, in the form used by `DriverParameters`
    83	(with `a = α₀`). -/
    84	theorem homog_params {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    85	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    86	    DriverParameters.Homog d alpha alpha0 :=
    87	  ⟨h.dim, h.alpha0_pos, h.alpha0_lt_one, by linarith [h.threshold], h.alpha_range⟩
    88	
    89	/-- `E:kappa` with the manuscript's hypothesis: under `H:homog`,
    90	`κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α) ∈ (1, 2)`. -/
    91	theorem kappa_mem_Ioo_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    92	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    93	    KappaRange.kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 :=
    94	  KappaRange.kappa_mem_Ioo d alpha alpha0 h.dim h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one
    95	    h.threshold h.alpha_range
    96	
    97	/-- `E:driver-parameters` with the manuscript's hypothesis (the section
    98	retains `H:homog` and sets `a = α₀`): its strict intervals are nonempty. -/
    99	theorem parameters_nonempty_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   100	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
   101	    ∃ γ θ β : ℝ, (0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ∧
   102	      (1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - alpha0 / 2) ((3 - alpha0 - alpha) / 2)) :=
   103	  DriverParameters.parameters_nonempty d alpha alpha0 (homog_params h)
   104	
   105	end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.HomogHypothesis

  2531	\begin{lemma}[Exact cutoffs for finite Gaussian words]\label{L:finite-word-cutoff}
  2532	  Let $g_{ij}$, $1 \le i \le M$, $1 \le j \le m_i$, be independent standard real
  2533	  Gaussian coordinates, grouped by color $i$, and let $\mathscr{X}$ be a complex
  2534	  Hilbert space. On Gaussian polynomials with coefficients in $\mathscr{X}$ set
  2535	  \[
  2536	    J_i=\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}M_{g_{ij}}\otimes K_{ij},
  2537	  \]
  2538	  where each $K_{ij}$ is bounded on $\mathscr{X}$. Let $F_0,\ldots,F_n$ be
  2539	  bounded operators acting only on $\mathscr{X}$. Fix a word $i_1,\ldots,i_n$,
  2540	  and let $r_i$ be the number of its occurrences of color $i$. If $N_i \ge r_i$
  2541	  and $P$ projects each color onto total Hermite degree at most $N_i$, then, for
  2542	  every $v \in \mathscr{X}$,
  2543	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-word-cutoff}
  2544	    \begin{split}
  2545	      &(I\otimes F_n)(PJ_{i_n}P)(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2546	      (PJ_{i_1}P)(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v)\\
  2547	      &\qquad=(I\otimes F_n)J_{i_n}(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2548	      J_{i_1}(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v).
  2549	    \end{split}
  2550	  \end{equation}
  2551	  The equality holds for finite sums and for Bochner integrals of such words
  2552	  whenever the displayed vector integrals exist.
  2553	\end{lemma}
  2554	
  2555	\begin{proof}
  2556	  In normalized Hermite coordinates, multiplication by $g_{ij}$ maps
  2557	  $h_{\boldsymbol a}$ to $\sqrt{a_{ij}+1}\,h_{\boldsymbol a+e_{ij}}
  2558	  +\sqrt{a_{ij}}\,h_{\boldsymbol a-e_{ij}}$; the second term is zero if $a_{ij}
  2559	  = 0$. Thus, it changes the total degree of color $i$ by one and leaves all
  2560	  other color degrees unchanged. The operators $I\otimes F_l$ leave every
  2561	  Gaussian degree unchanged. After the first $l$ insertions, the uncompressed
  2562	  word therefore has color-$i$ degree at most $r_i(l) = |\{j\le l:i_j=i\}| \le
  2563	  r_i \le N_i$. This is an induction starting from degree zero in every color.
  2564	  Consequently, $P$ is the identity both before and after every insertion along
  2565	  that word. Induction on $l$ now proves \eqref{E:finite-word-cutoff}. The
  2566	  lowering term has been retained: the assertion includes creation followed by
  2567	  annihilation and all resulting self-contractions. Linearity and equality of
  2568	  the vector integrands prove the last assertion. This is an equality of
  2569	  selected finite words, not of full propagators at a fixed cutoff. This proves
  2570	  Lemma~\ref{L:finite-word-cutoff}.
  2571	\end{proof}

  2577	\begin{proposition}[All regularized static phase orders]
  2578	  \label{P:static-phase-all-orders}

  2582	  an ordinary Gaussian polynomial of degree at most $n$, including
  2583	  self-contractions; it is not a pure Wick chaos. There is an explicit finite
  2584	  constant

  2591	    \le
  2592	    \frac{(A_\alpha\sqrt{R_\alpha})^n
  2593	    h^{(4-\alpha)n/2}}{(n!)^{(3-\alpha)/2}}
  2594	    \|(f,g)\|_{1/h}.
  2595	  \end{equation}

  2597	  $\sum_{n\ge0}\sigma^nZ_n^\epsilon(h)$ converges in $L^2$ phase. Its squared
  2598	  norm is at most
  2599	  \begin{equation}\label{E:all-static-phase-sum}
  2600	    (\sqrt e+2)^2
  2601	    \exp\left\{6A_\alpha^{2/(3-\alpha)}
  2602	    (|\sigma|^2R_\alpha)^{1/(3-\alpha)}
  2603	    h^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}\right\}\|(f,g)\|_{1/h}^2.
  2604	  \end{equation}

  2621	    \left(\frac{d_N}
  2622	    {\delta_{\alpha/2}\lambda^{2-\alpha/2}}\right)^n

  2632	  Choose $\lambda = n/h$. For any phase $z$, $\|z\|_{1/h} \le n\|z\|_{n/h}$ and

    22	
    23	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian envelope for the original covariance]
    24	  \label{L:variational-heat-envelope}
    25	  For the normalized heat kernel $p_\epsilon(x) =
    26	  (2\pi\epsilon)^{-d/2}e^{-|x|^2/(2\epsilon)}$,
    27	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-heat-envelope}
    28	    (\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    29	    =\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}\mu(\ud\xi),
    30	    \qquad
    31	    0\le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    32	    \le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(0)<\infty.
    33	  \end{equation}
    34	  The value at zero is strictly positive.
    35	\end{lemma}
    36	
    37	\begin{proof}
    38	  A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial ball growth. Indeed, evaluate
    39	  its tempered bound on a nonnegative smooth cutoff equal to one on $B_1$,
    40	  dilated by $R \ge 1$. Its finitely many Schwartz seminorms are bounded by
    41	  $CR^N$, so positivity gives a ball-mass bound $CR^N$. Summing dyadic annuli
    42	  shows that $(1+|x|)^{-L}$ is integrable for $L > N$. Apply this separately to
    43	  $\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Gaussian weights are therefore integrable against both
    44	  measures. The classical convolution on the left is finite and smooth locally
    45	  in $x$: on compact $x$ sets its translated Gaussian derivatives are bounded by
    46	  any fixed sufficiently fast polynomial weight in the integration variable.
    47	
    48	  Pair the convolution with a Schwartz test $\varphi$. Absolute Fubini is
    49	  justified by these weights. The resulting pairing is that of $\Gamma$ with
    50	  $p_\epsilon*\varphi$. Applying the spectral convention in
    51	  Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} and the identity $\int p_\epsilon(y)e^{-i\xi\cdot
    52	  y}\ud y = e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}$ gives exactly the right side
    53	  of~\eqref{E:variational-heat-envelope} as a distribution. The heat kernel is
    54	  even, so either Fourier sign gives that same Gaussian multiplier. Its spectral
    55	  integral is absolutely finite and continuous in $x$ by dominated convergence.
    56	  Thus, equality of the two continuous distributions gives equality at every
    57	  $x$, without an extra normalization factor. The physical convolution is
    58	  nonnegative. Evenness of $\mu$ makes the spectral integral real, and its
    59	  absolute value is bounded by its total Gaussian mass, the value at zero.
    60	  Finally, $\Gamma \ne 0$ and $p_\epsilon > 0$ give strict positivity there.
    61	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope}.
    62	\end{proof}

    64	\begin{lemma}[Global regularity of the original mean]
    65	  \label{L:variational-global-mean}
    66	  Every mixed time and space derivative of $h_s$ is globally bounded in space,
    67	  uniformly on compact time intervals. In particular, for $I = [0,1]$ there are
    68	  finite constants $M,C_\Psi$ such that
    69	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-global-mean}
    70	    0\le h_s(x)\le M,\qquad
    71	    \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty\le C_\Psi|s-t|,
    72	    \qquad s,t\in I.
    73	  \end{equation}
    74	\end{lemma}
    75	
    76	\begin{proof}
    77	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time; its compact support inside $(0,1)$ makes this a
    78	  smooth extension. For any mixed derivative $D\Psi$, a fixed $\epsilon > 0$ and
    79	  compactness of its common spatial support give $|D\Psi(t,x)| \le
    80	  C_Dp_\epsilon(x)$ for all $t,x$. Here the heat kernel has a positive minimum
    81	  on that support. Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope} consequently bounds
    82	  $\Gamma*|D\Psi(t,\cdot)|$ uniformly in $t,x$. Ordinary local differentiation
    83	  against the Radon measure gives the corresponding derivatives of the
    84	  convolution. After the change $r = s-t$,
    85	  \[
    86	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
    87	    (\Gamma*\Psi(s-r,\cdot))(x)\ud r.
    88	  \]
    89	  For $s$ in a compact interval the relevant $r$ lie in a fixed bounded
    90	  interval. The preceding global bound times $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable since $a <
    91	  1$. Every derivative thus falls on the smooth test and passes through the
    92	  integral by dominated convergence, with the claimed global spatial bounds.
    93	  Nonnegativity follows from positive kernels. The bounded time derivative
    94	  proves the Lipschitz estimate. No directional decay of the mean has been
    95	  inferred. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-global-mean}.
    96	\end{proof}

    98	\begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
    99	  \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
   100	  On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
   101	  $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
   102	  h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
   103	  positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
   104	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
   105	    \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
   106	    =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   107	    \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	  It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
   110	  positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
   111	\end{proposition}
   112	
   113	\begin{proof}
   114	  The Fourier Laplacian $A = -\Delta$ is self-adjoint on $H^2$, being
   115	  multiplication by $|\xi|^2$ with its maximal domain. Multiplication $B_s =
   116	  -h_s$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm at most $M$. Thus, $H_s = A+B_s$ is
   117	  densely defined, symmetric and closed on $H^2$; the two graph norms are
   118	  equivalent under a bounded perturbation. For real $b > M$,
   119	  \[
   120	    H_s-ib=(I+B_s(A-ib)^{-1})(A-ib).
   121	  \]
   122	  The first factor has a Neumann inverse because $\|B_s(A-ib)^{-1}\| \le M/b <
   123	  1$, and the same holds with $+ib$. To check self-adjointness directly, for $u
   124	  \in D(H_s^*)$ solve $(H_s-ib)v = (H_s^*-ib)u$ with $v \in D(H_s)$. Then $u-v
   125	  \in \ker(H_s^*-ib) = \operatorname{Ran}(H_s+ib)^\perp = \{0\}$. Hence,
   126	  $D(H_s^*) = D(H_s)$.
   127	
   128	  Set $c_{\mathrm{shift}} = 1+M$ and $J_s = H_s+c_{\mathrm{shift}} \ge 1$.
   129	  Integration by parts on $H^2$ gives
   130	  \[
   131	    \|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2=q_s(f)+c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_2^2,\qquad
   132	    \|f\|_{H^1}^2\le\|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2
   133	    \le c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_{H^1}^2.
   134	  \]
   135	  Spectral cutoffs $1_{[1,n]}(J_s)$ show that $H^2 = D(J_s)$ is a core for the
   136	  half-power norm; Fourier cutoffs give its density in $H^1$. Completion in the
   137	  equivalent norms identifies $D(J_s^{1/2})$ and $H^1$ as $L^2$ subspaces, since
   138	  both norms dominate $L^2$. This proves the stated form domain.
   139	
   140	  The spectral lower bound gives one direction of the Rayleigh identity. For the
   141	  reverse, nonzero spectral projections in $[E_s,E_s+\epsilon]$ give unit $H^2$
   142	  vectors with Rayleigh values at most $E_s+\epsilon$. The bottom is finite
   143	  because the operator is bounded below and has finite Rayleigh tests. Let
   144	  $\epsilon\downarrow0$. Real tests give the same infimum: $q_s(u+iv) =
   145	  q_s(u)+q_s(v)$, so the quotient is the norm-weighted average of the nonzero
   146	  real quotients. This proves the Rayleigh identity with $-E_s$ on the left. The
   147	  following negative upper bound justifies writing that value as
   148	  $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2$ in~\eqref{E:variational-real-rayleigh}.
   149	
   150	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-original-common-trial} supplies, for this original
   151	  $\Psi$, one unit compactly supported $w$ and a finite plateau mask with a
   152	  common strictly negative upper bound $\epsilon_0 > 0$. Its trial has support
   153	  in $B_{2L}$; choose its plateau radius $R_0 \ge 2L$. The unmasked form on this
   154	  same $w$ is no larger. Consequently, $-M \le E_s \le -\epsilon_0 < 0$, and
   155	  $\sqrt{\epsilon_0} \le \lambda_{\Psi,s} \le \sqrt M$. Comparing identical unit
   156	  form tests gives $|E_s-E_t| \le \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty$ and therefore
   157	  \[
   158	    |\lambda_{\Psi,s}-\lambda_{\Psi,t}|
   159	    \le \frac{C_\Psi}{2\sqrt{\epsilon_0}}|s-t|.
   160	  \]
   161	  This also proves positivity and finiteness of $I_\Psi$. No compact-potential
   162	  spectral theorem was applied to $H_s$. This proves
   163	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate}.
   164	\end{proof}

   166	\subsection{Removing masks from the numerical lower rate}
   167	
   168	\begin{proposition}[Monotone rates and the original point moment]
   169	  \label{P:variational-remove-mask}
   170	  There is an increasing family of admissible radial masks $m_R$ tending to one,
   171	  for which the compact ground rates satisfy
   172	  $\lambda_{R,s}\uparrow\lambda_{\Psi,s}$ uniformly on $I$ as $R \to \infty$,
   173	  with the compact ground statements used for $R \ge R_0(\Psi)$. For the
   174	  original canonical solution and any fixed $x$,
   175	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-unmasked-point-lower}
   176	    \liminf_{T\to\infty}T^{-\kappa}\log\E|u(T,x)|^2
   177	    \ge2I_\Psi-\frac{v_\Psi}{2}.
   178	  \end{equation}
   179	\end{proposition}
   180	
   181	\begin{proof}
   182	  Put $F(t) = e^{-1/t}$ for $t > 0$ and zero otherwise, and define
   183	  \[
   184	    \chi(r)=\frac{F(2-r)}{F(2-r)+F(r-1)},\qquad
   185	    m_R(x)=\chi(|x|/R).
   186	  \]
   187	  The denominator is positive. The numerator decreases and the second
   188	  denominator term increases; thus $\chi$ is nonincreasing, equals one on $r \le
   189	  1$, and zero on $r \ge 2$. Flatness of $F$ at zero gives smoothness. Since
   190	  $\chi$ is constant near zero, $m_R$ is smooth also at the spatial origin.
   191	  These even $[0,1]$ masks increase pointwise to one.
   192	
   193	  Choose $R_0$ so the preceding common trial lies in the plateau. Every $R \ge
   194	  R_0$ has the same negative margin. For each fixed $R$, the compact-family
   195	  theorem applies to $m_Rh_s$. Its real Rayleigh formula follows from the same
   196	  real/complex quotient argument as~\eqref{E:variational-real-rayleigh}. The
   197	  rates are continuous, positive, at most $\sqrt M$ and monotone in $R$. For
   198	  every fixed real unit $f \in H^1$, dominated convergence gives $\int m_Rh_sf^2
   199	  \to \int h_sf^2$. Hence,
   200	  \[
   201	    \sup_{R\ge R_0}\lambda_{R,s}^2
   202	    =\sup_{\|f\|_2=1,\ f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)}
   203	    \sup_{R\ge R_0}
   204	    \left(\int m_Rh_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right)
   205	    =\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2.
   206	  \]
   207	  Only two numerical suprema were interchanged. Positive square roots give the
   208	  pointwise rate convergence. For $R_n = R_0+n$ and $\epsilon > 0$, the
   209	  increasing open sets $\{s:\lambda_{\Psi,s}-\lambda_{R_n,s}<\epsilon\}$ cover
   210	  compact $I$. A finite subcover lies in the largest one, proving uniform
   211	  convergence. Monotonicity extends it to all real $R \to \infty$. Therefore,
   212	  $\int_I\lambda_{R,s}\ud s\uparrow I_\Psi$.
   213	
   214	  At each fixed $R$ use this very same mask in the operator path and mean when
   215	  applying Proposition~\ref{P:raw-block-original-lower}. It gives the lower
   216	  bound with $2\int_I\lambda_{R,s}\ud s-v_\Psi/2$ for the same original point
   217	  liminf. Taking the numerical supremum over these individual bounds proves
   218	  \eqref{E:variational-unmasked-point-lower}. There is no $R(T)$, unmasked noisy
   219	  wave, uniform-in-mask Gaussian estimate or exchange of source and time limits.
   220	  This proves Proposition~\ref{P:variational-remove-mask}.
   221	\end{proof}

   223	\subsection{Full-class dilation and finite variational values for nonnegative controls}
   224	
   225	\begin{lemma}[Radon and Rayleigh dilation]\label{L:variational-control-dilation}
   226	  For $r > 0$ the map
   227	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-control-dilation}
   228	    (D_r\Psi)(s,x)=r^{d+2-\alpha}\Psi(s,rx)
   229	  \end{equation}
   230	  is a bijection of $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$, with inverse $D_{1/r}$. With
   231	  the same original covariance,
   232	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-dilation-values}
   233	    h_{D_r\Psi,s}(x)=r^2h_{\Psi,s}(rx),\qquad
   234	    v_{D_r\Psi}=r^{4-\alpha}v_\Psi,\qquad
   235	    \lambda_{D_r\Psi,s}=r\lambda_{\Psi,s},\quad
   236	    I_{D_r\Psi}=rI_\Psi.
   237	  \end{equation}
   238	\end{lemma}
   239	
   240	\begin{proof}
   241	  Positive dilation preserves the full smooth positive nonzero class;
   242	  multiplication of its amplitude powers gives the stated inverse. Homogeneity
   243	  of the physical Radon measure gives, for every nonnegative measurable $G$,
   244	  \[
   245	    \int G(ry)\Gamma(\ud y)
   246	    =r^{\alpha-d}\int G(z)\Gamma(\ud z).
   247	  \]
   248	  Indeed, its left pushforward measure on a Borel set $A$ is $\Gamma(A/r) =
   249	  r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$. Positive Tonelli applies this identity inside the
   250	  temporal convolution, giving $h_{D_r\Psi,s}(x) = r^2h_{\Psi,s}(rx)$. Now use
   251	  the \emph{Lebesgue} substitution $z = rx$ in the original pairing:
   252	  \[
   253	    v_{D_r\Psi}=r^{d+2-\alpha}r^2r^{-d}v_\Psi
   254	    =r^{4-\alpha}v_\Psi.
   255	  \]
   256	  This distinguishes the Radon pushforward from the spatial volume factor; it
   257	  includes singular covariances and white noise.
   258	
   259	  The map $U_rf(x) = r^{d/2}f(rx)$ is a unitary bijection on real $L^2$,
   260	  preserving $H^1,H^2$ as sets under its inverse. Weak derivatives give
   261	  $\|\nabla U_rf\|_2^2 = r^2\|\nabla f\|_2^2$ and $\int h_{D_r\Psi,s}(U_rf)^2 =
   262	  r^2\int h_{\Psi,s}f^2$. The real Rayleigh bijection proves the squared rate
   263	  identity; the rates are positive, so their square roots and integrals give
   264	  \eqref{E:variational-dilation-values}. On $H^2$ this is also $H_{D_r\Psi,s}U_r
   265	  = r^2U_rH_{\Psi,s}$. Time has not been rescaled. For compact masks the
   266	  corresponding identity uses $m_R(rx) = m_{R/r}(x)$; a fixed mask radius is not
   267	  invariant. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation}.
   268	\end{proof}

   270	\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic variational lower bounds]
   271	  \label{P:variational-positive-scores}
   272	  For $c > 0$, the set of variational values
   273	  $\{cI_\Psi-v_\Psi/2:\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}\}$ is nonempty and
   274	  bounded above. Its finite real supremum $S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is positive and
   275	  satisfies
   276	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-homogeneity}
   277	    S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}=c^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}},
   278	    \qquad
   279	    Q_2\ge S_2^{\mathrm{pos}},
   280	  \end{equation}
   281	  where $Q_2$ is the original point liminf. The coefficient-one value is an
   282	  auxiliary variational value; no first-moment or source-constant identification
   283	  is asserted.
   284	\end{proposition}
   285	
   286	\begin{proof}
   287	  Write $k = 3-\alpha > 0$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $m = q/k > 1$. Fix one
   288	  $\Psi_0$ from the nonempty class and put $I_0 = I_{\Psi_0} > 0$, $v_0 =
   289	  v_{\Psi_0} > 0$. Positivity of the latter is
   290	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}. For $r_0 = (I_0/v_0)^{1/k} > 0$, which need
   291	  not be less than one, the exact real-power identity gives
   292	  \[
   293	    I_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}-v_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}/2
   294	    =r_0I_0-r_0^qv_0/2=r_0I_0/2>0.
   295	  \]
   296	  This positive value is obtained from a smooth nonnegative control.
   297	
   298	  For $c > 0$ put $r_c = c^{1/k}$ and $K_c = c^m > 0$.
   299	  Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation} and the exact scalar powers give,
   300	  for every $\Psi$,
   301	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-set-scaling}
   302	    cI_{D_{r_c}\Psi}-v_{D_{r_c}\Psi}/2
   303	    =K_c(I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2).
   304	  \end{equation}
   305	  Since $D_{r_c}$ is a bijection of the entire class, the whole set of
   306	  variational values with coefficient $c$ is $K_c$ times the whole
   307	  coefficient-one set of variational values.
   308	
   309	  We prove boundedness before taking finite-real suprema. The independent
   310	  Theorem~\ref{T:full-upper}, for the \emph{same canonical solution}, gives
   311	  \[
   312	    \E|u(T,0)|^2\le e(T+2)^d e^{C_{\mathrm{up}}T^\kappa},
   313	    \qquad T\ge1,\quad C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty.
   314	  \]

   316	  (T^\epsilon-1)/\epsilon$ and $\log(T+2) \le \log T+\log3$ for $T \ge 1$, and
   317	  divide by $T^\kappa$. Thus, the original point limsup is at most
   318	  $C_{\mathrm{up}}$. One fixed test/mask lower bound gives a finite lower bound

   322	  Equation~\eqref{E:variational-score-set-scaling} at $c = 2$ consequently
   323	  bounds all coefficient-one variational values by $C_{\mathrm{up}}/K_2$. The
   324	  nonempty set has a finite real supremum $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} > 0$ by the

   327	  For general $c$, set equality and $K_c > 0$ show that $K_cS_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   328	  is the supremum: it is an upper bound, and every smaller number is exceeded by
   329	  $K_c$ times a coefficient-one variational expression within the corresponding
   330	  positive distance of its supremum. This proves finiteness, positivity and the
   331	  first identity in~\eqref{E:variational-score-homogeneity}. Taking the

   335	  improvement without a first-moment identification. This proves
   336	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
   337	\end{proof}

    23	\begin{lemma}[Full-profile squares in the original space]
    24	  \label{L:occupation-raw-square}
    25	  There is a continuous map $Q:H^1(\R^d;\R) \to H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ with
    26	  \[
    27	    \langle Q(f),Q(h)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    28	    =B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2),\qquad
    29	    \|Q(f)\|^2=A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f).

    31	  For $g \in \mathcal{O}$, the element $\rho_g = J_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}(s\mapsto
    32	  Q(g_s))$ belongs to the original $H_I$ and satisfies
    33	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-raw-identities}
    34	    \|\rho_g\|_{H_I}^2=A(g),\qquad
    35	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle_{H_I}
    36	    =\int_I\int_{\R^d}h_{\Psi,s}(x)g_s(x)^2\ud x\ud s
    37	  \end{equation}
    38	  for every $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$. In particular,
    39	  \[
    40	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle_{H_I}\le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g)}.

    44	\begin{proof}
    45	  Approximate $f$ in $H^1$ by real compact smooth $f_n$.
    46	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} gives
    47	  \[
    48	    \|f_n^2-f_l^2\|_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}^2
    49	    =C_4(f_n-f_l,f_n+f_l,f_n-f_l,f_n+f_l)
    50	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}N(f_n-f_l)^2N(f_n+f_l)^2\to0.
    51	  \]

    53	  defines $Q(f)$; interlacing two approximating sequences proves independence.
    54	  Passing the physical four-linear continuity and Hilbert pairings to limits
    55	  proves the first identities. The same difference bound, first for smooth

   116	  it constant, and an $L^2$ constant on $\R^d$ is zero. Hence, $0 < T(g) <

   119	  concavity, proves

   124	  $\mathcal{O}$ and has positive $A$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.

   127	  The map $(U_\ell g)_s(x) = \ell^{d/2}g_s(\ell x)$ is an $H^1$ isomorphism
   128	  preserving unit mass and strong measurability. It has inverse $U_{1/\ell}$ and
   129	  is a bijection on $\mathcal{O}$. The physical Radon change of variables gives
   130	  \[
   131	    A(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A(g),\qquad
   132	    T(U_\ell g)=\ell^2T(g).
   133	  \]

   135	  $\ell^{-d}$, and the pushforward of $\Gamma$ contributes $\ell^{\alpha-d}$.

   137	  $g,\ell$ leaves the class unchanged. For fixed $A,T > 0$, the derivative of
   138	  $A\ell^\alpha-\zeta T\ell^2$ has the sign of $\alpha A-2\zeta
   139	  T\ell^{2-\alpha}$. Its global maximum occurs at $\ell = (\alpha A/(2\zeta
   140	  T))^{1/(2-\alpha)}$ and equals $D_\zeta[A/T^{\alpha/2}]^{2/(2-\alpha)}$. For

   142	  $C_{\rm occ}$ gives one inequality in~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-energy}. Fixed
   143	  ratios approaching its positive supremum give the other by continuity of the
   144	  positive power. Algebra gives~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-ratio} and the penalty
   145	  scaling. No optimizer or minimax interchange is assumed. This proves

   149	\begin{lemma}[Countable Rayleigh near-occupations]
   150	  \label{L:occupation-rayleigh-selection}
   151	  For fixed $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$
   152	  there is $g_\varepsilon \in \mathcal{O}$ such that
   153	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-rayleigh-selection}
   154	    I_\Psi^2+T(g_\varepsilon)
   155	    \le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g_\varepsilon)}+\varepsilon .
   156	  \end{equation}

   159	\begin{proof}
   160	  The real $H^1$ space is separable, for example by its isometric embedding
   161	  $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ into a finite product of $L^2$ spaces. Compact smooth
   162	  density therefore supplies a countable real family. Discard zero and normalize
   163	  each member in $L^2$ to obtain $f_j$ dense in the $L^2$-unit $H^1$ class.
   164	  Normalization preserves convergence because the approximating $L^2$ norms tend
   165	  to one. Put $b_j = \|\nabla f_j\|_2^2$ and $R_j(s) = \int
   166	  h_{\Psi,s}f_j^2-b_j$. Bounded-potential form continuity and
   167	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} give $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2 =
   168	  \sup_jR_j(s)$. The canonical functions are measurable, indeed continuous. Let
   169	  $U_j = \{s:R_j(s)>\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2-\varepsilon\}$, $A_1 = U_1$ and $A_j =
   170	  U_j\setminus\bigcup_{i<j}U_i$. These first-index cells are Borel and cover
   171	  $I$. Put $g_\varepsilon(s) = f_j$ on $A_j$. Finite-valued truncations using
   172	  $f_1$ on the remaining cells converge pointwise in $H^1$, proving strong
   173	  measurability. A null-set representative may be filled by $f_1$.

   175	  With $H_\Psi = \sup_{s,x}h_{\Psi,s}(x) < \infty$, the selection implies
   176	  \[
   177	    b(g_\varepsilon(s))
   178	    <\int h_{\Psi,s}g_\varepsilon(s)^2-\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2+\varepsilon
   179	    \le H_\Psi+\varepsilon .
   180	  \]

   182	  inequality, using Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-raw-square}, gives
   183	  \[
   184	    \int_I\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2\ud s+T(g_\varepsilon)
   185	    \le\langle\Psi,\rho_{g_\varepsilon}\rangle+\varepsilon
   186	    \le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g_\varepsilon)}+\varepsilon .
   187	  \]

   189	  \int_I\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2\ud s$. This

   191	  selector or limiting occupation is required. This proves
   192	  Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-rayleigh-selection}.

   224	  Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-rayleigh-selection} gives $I_\Psi^2 \le
   225	  \sqrt{vC}T^\beta-T+\varepsilon$ for some $T > 0$. Bound it by the supremum

   227	  supremum is zero. If $v > 0$, the derivative $\beta\sqrt{vC}T^{\beta-1}-1$

   423	  Lipschitz in $\sigma$ in $L^\infty$ and $L^2$.

   428	  original covariance identity and absolute Fubini give the stated mean pairing:
   429	  the two compact tests restrict spatial differences to a compact set of finite
   430	  $\Gamma$ mass, and the time singularity is locally integrable since $a < 1$.
   431	  This identifies the linear covariance mean without evaluating noise at a
   432	  point. The same calculation gives~\eqref{E:compact-raw-cost}. Its spatial
   433	  integrand is bounded in integral by
   434	  $\|\Psi\|_\infty^2|B_A|\Gamma(\overline{B}_{2A})$, and
   435	  $\int_0^1\int_0^1|\sigma-u|^{-a}\ud u\ud\sigma = 2/((1-a)(2-a))$, proving
   436	  finiteness.

   439	  0$. Nonzero $\Gamma$ charges some ball, and homogeneity gives $\Gamma(B_1) =
   440	  r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(B_r) > 0$. Thus, every origin-centered ball $B_r$, $r > 0$,
   441	  has positive finite mass. The continuous compact autocorrelation
   442	  $\int\overline{q}(x)\overline{q}(x-z)\ud x$ is positive at zero and bounded
   443	  below on some ball. This proves $0 < Q(\overline{q}) < \infty$. Since
   444	  $|\sigma-u|^{-a} \ge 1$ on the unit time square, positive Tonelli gives both
   445	  inequalities in~\eqref{E:compact-positive-mean-floor}.
   446	
   447	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time and write
   448	  \[
   449	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
   450	    \int\Gamma(\ud z)\Psi(s-r,x-z)\ud r.
   451	  \]

   453	  $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable there. Every derivative falls on the smooth test, not
   454	  on the singular time kernel. Dominated differentiation gives smoothness and
   455	  continuity of all derivatives on compacts. Multiplication by $m_R$ now gives

   457	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}.

   460	\begin{proposition}[Binding with the original control and cost fixed]
   461	  \label{P:compact-original-common-trial}
   462	  For every $\Psi$ in Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}, a sufficiently large
   463	  finite mask $m_R$ gives $V_\sigma = m_Rh_\sigma$ a common negative
   464	  trial~\eqref{E:compact-common-trial}. Thus, all preceding ground, projection,
   465	  positive-margin and complementary-wave conclusions apply. The rate is
   466	  Lipschitz on $I$ and has $\lambda_0 > 0$. The original test $\Psi$, original
   467	  variable $Z$ and variance $v_\Psi$ are unchanged by this choice. The mask can
   468	  additionally cover any fixed compact variational test supports.

   472	  Choose a real unit $L^2$ function $\psi \in C_c^\infty(B_2)$ with $\psi \ge
   473	  c_0 > 0$ on $B_1$, and put $\psi_L(x) = L^{-d/2}\psi(x/L)$, $D_\psi =
   474	  \|\nabla\psi\|_2^2$, where $L \ge \max(1,2A)$. Choose the even mask with $R
   475	  \ge 2L$, so $V_\sigma = h_\sigma$ on $\operatorname{supp}\psi_L$. This is the
   476	  allowed real mask $0 \le m_R \le 1$, equal to one on $B_R$ and with support in
   477	  $\overline{B}_{2R}$. Positive Tonelli
   478	  and~\eqref{E:compact-positive-mean-floor} give
   479	  \begin{align}
   480	    \int V_\sigma\psi_L^2
   481	    &\ge c_0^2L^{-d}\int_{B_L}(\Gamma*\overline{q})(x)\ud x\nonumber\\
   482	    &=c_0^2L^{-d}\int\overline{q}(y)\Gamma(B_L-y)\ud y\nonumber\\
   483	    &\ge c_0^2L^{-d}\Gamma(B_{L/2})\int\overline{q}
   484	    =C_\Gamma L^{-\alpha},\label{E:compact-trial-potential}\\
   485	    C_\Gamma&=c_0^22^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(B_1)\int\overline{q}>0.\nonumber
   486	  \end{align}

   488	  masses in the argument are compact and finite. The kinetic energy is $D_\psi
   489	  L^{-2}$. Since $\alpha < 2$, choose $L$ large enough that $\varepsilon_R: =
   490	  C_\Gamma L^{-\alpha}-D_\psi L^{-2} > 0$. Then
   491	  \[
   492	    \|\nabla\psi_L\|_2^2-\int V_\sigma\psi_L^2
   493	    \le-\varepsilon_R\quad\hbox{for every }\sigma\in I.
   494	  \]

   496	  Its level bound and the mean Lipschitz estimate give
   497	  \[
   498	    |\lambda_\sigma-\lambda_\tau|
   499	    \le\frac{\|V_\sigma-V_\tau\|_\infty}{2\sqrt{\varepsilon_R}}
   500	    \le C_R|\sigma-\tau|.

   503	  though $\Psi(0,\cdot) = 0$. Only the trial and mask have grown; the original
   504	  test, its variable and~\eqref{E:compact-raw-cost} were fixed first. Enlarging
   505	  $R$ to contain additional fixed compact test supports preserves the trial and
   506	  gives equality of masked and unmasked potential energies on those supports.

   508	  white case. It is not an all-strength binding assertion for one fixed compact
   509	  potential. Masks are fixed before source or time asymptotics; a later supremum
   510	  over controls must follow their individual bounds. This proves
   511	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-original-common-trial}.

   301	  \label{P:spatial-energy-map}

   303	  \[
   304	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   305	    =\sup_{\|g\|_2=1}

   331	  $\ell^\alpha A-\ell^2b/2$ occurs at $\ell^{2-\alpha} = \alpha A/b$ and equals

   331	\begin{theorem}[Intrinsic original second-moment constant]
   332	  \label{T:intrinsic-second-moment}
   333	  For every original admissible model with data $(1,0)$ and fixed $x$,
   334	  \begin{equation}\label{E:intrinsic-second-moment-limit}
   335	    \lim_{T\to\infty}T^{-(4-\alpha-a)/(3-\alpha)}
   336	    \log\E|u_\Gamma(T,x)|^2
   337	    =C_2(\Gamma,a)=S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}
   338	    =2^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}.
   339	  \end{equation}
   340	  Its complete variational formula over nonnegative controls is
   341	  \begin{align}
   342	    C_2(\Gamma,a)
   343	    &=\sup_{\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}}
   344	    \left\{2\int_I
   345	    \sqrt{\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   346	    \left(\int h_{\Psi,s}f^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right)}
   347	    \ud s-\frac{v_\Psi}{2}\right\},
   348	    \label{E:intrinsic-positive-formula}\\
   349	    h_{\Psi,s}(x)
   350	    &=\int_I|s-t|^{-a}(\Gamma*\Psi_t)(x)\ud t,\qquad
   351	    v_\Psi=\int_{I\times\R^d}\Psi(s,x)h_{\Psi,s}(x)\ud x\ud s.
   352	    \notag
   353	  \end{align}

   355	  $C_c^\infty(I\times\R^d)$ tests, including nonseparable ones. The covariance
   356	  retains its amplitude, the kinetic term has coefficient one, and the Gaussian
   357	  action is $v_\Psi/2$. For nonzero covariance $0 < C_2 < \infty$. For $\Gamma =
   358	  0$ the constant and moment rate are zero.
   359	\end{theorem}

   361	\begin{proof}
   362	  Assume first $\Gamma \ne 0$. Proposition~\ref{P:original-signed-point-upper},
   363	  followed by Proposition~\ref{P:positive-score-cutoff} with $R =
   364	  \delta^{-1}+2$, bounds the original point limsup by $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}$.
   365	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores} bounds the original point
   366	  liminf below by this same value. Both are for the same canonical Stratonovich
   367	  solution, exponent, original covariance and variance-half action. Their with
   368	  the regularization removed first identifications retain all mixed, unequal,
   369	  self and empty chains and both phase components with initial data $(1,0)$. The
   370	  original spatial stationarity proved in
   371	  Proposition~\ref{P:raw-block-original-lower} extends both bounds to every
   372	  fixed $x$. Thus, the limit exists and equals $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}$. Its
   373	  homogeneity, positivity and finiteness are
   374	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.

   381	\end{proof}

  4292	## SeriesType (whole result)
  4293	
  4294	Elementary scalar facts that `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  4295	(main file, at `a284420`) uses inline inside proofs, plus one standalone
  4296	Gamma-function tool (`gamma_mid_sq_le`) for which no manuscript line is
  4297	claimed. None of them is a labelled result. Everything is proved and nothing is supplied as a
  4298	hypothesis. The module contains:
  4299	
  4300	- the finite `ell^nu` inequality `sum a_k^nu <= (sum a_k)^nu` for `nu >= 1`
  4301	  and `a_k >= 0`;
  4302	- the series bound `S_nu(x) = sum_k x^k/(k!)^nu <= exp(nu x^(1/nu))` for
  4303	  `nu >= 1` and `x >= 0`, with summability as part of the conclusion (a Lean
  4304	  `tsum` of a non-summable family is `0`);
  4305	- the `beta < 1` Hoelder variant of the proof of `P:static-phase-all-orders`
  4306	  (lines 2670-2679): `sum x^n/(n!)^beta <= 2^(1-beta) exp(2 beta x^(1/beta))`
  4307	  for `1/2 <= beta < 1`, proved by the TeX's own Hoelder factorization, and
  4308	  the displayed bound `<= 2 e^(3x^(1/beta))` for every `1/2 <= beta <= 3`;
  4309	  the TeX needs it only at `beta = (3-alpha)/2 in (1/2, 3/2)`;
  4310	- `(k!)^2 <= r! s!` when `r + s = 2k` (lines 2754, 5119);
  4311	- the two-sided bound `k log k - k + 1 <= log k! <= k log k - k + 1 + log k`
  4312	  for `k >= 1`, a step of the proof of `L:positive-series-type`
  4313	  (lines 7244-7247);
  4314	- `Gamma((x+y)/2)^2 <= Gamma(x) Gamma(y)` (the standalone tool; its row has
  4315	  its own label "no direct label (SeriesType foundation: standalone Gamma
  4316	  tool, no manuscript line claimed)").
  4317	
  4318	The powers `(k!)^nu` with real `nu` are `Real.rpow` of the positive real `k!`,
  4319	so no junk value of `rpow` enters. Proof-route differences:
  4320	
  4321	- The factorial bounds are proved by induction on `k` with `1 + x <= e^x`
  4322	  (`factorial_ge_exp`, `factorial_le_exp`, auxiliary), not by the TeX's

  4324	- `(k!)^2 <= r! s!` is proved through the central binomial coefficient; the
  4325	  TeX gives no proof.
